definition: The number of nuclei in a radioactive sample that decay per unit time, measured in becquerels (1 Bq is one decay per second).
The number of counts a detector records per unit time; the part due to a source is less than the source's activity because the detector catches only some of its radiation.
The time taken for the number of undecayed nuclei of a nuclide, or its activity, to fall to half; it is the same whatever the starting amount.
Radiation that is always present from sources such as radon gas, rocks, cosmic rays and food; subtract it from a measured count rate to find the count rate from a source.
